newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl against changes in EMU schedule, criteria.
newsitem.headline: Kohl against changes in EMU schedule, criteria.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Tuesday that he was opposed to any changes either in the timetable for European monetary union (EMU) or in the criteria determining which countries may join.
The launch of the euro currency is planned in 1999, and the fitness of countries to join will be judged early next year on the basis of their economic and budget results this year.

Speaking in Berlin, Kohl ruled out any delay in the EMU schedule, as well as a softening of the Maastricht convergence criteria. The treaty sets a budget deficit qualifying limit of three percent of gross domestic product.
"The stability criteria have absolute priority over the timetable," Kohl told reporters, adding: "The criteria cannot be softened because of the timetable."
Kohl declined to comment on which countries he expected to be in the starting lineup for monetary union, saying the number of participants would only be set in early 1998.

Although Kohl gave no clues on who would be likely to join EMU, other government leaders in Bonn have said that countries like Italy would not be ready to join at the outset, and should wait even if they qualify on paper.
Kohl, who meets Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi this Friday in Bonn, was asked by reporters what message he had for his counterpart over Italy's chances of joining EMU.
He replied: "Our Italian friends have the same problems as the Germans. They must do their homework. I'll tell my friend Prodi that you'll have to do your homework. We do too."
